To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the weathering indices of natural rocks are applicable to MSWI bottom ash for the evaluation of the weathering of MSWI bottom ash.
mineralogical weather indices for natural rock could be applicable as an index to identify fresh and landfilled municipal solid waste incinreration (MSWI) bottom ash.
the weathering of municipal waste incineration residue is complicated and difficult to describe leached concentrations of major and trace element.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of weathering indices to MSWI bottom ash for the first time.
the applicability of mineralogical weather indices to evaluate the weathering of municipal waste incineration residues.
the application of weathering indices to MSWI bottom ash for the purpose of evaluating the weathering of MSWI bottom ash in landfills.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mineralogical weather indices are not useful for describing the weathering of MSWI bottom ash quantitatively.
weathering indices for rock profiles are not applicable as an indicator for leachate pH or leaching concentration of component elements.

weathering indices for MSWI bottom ash are useful for the identification and estimation of weathering time but are not sufficient to predict leaching behavior of component elements in MSWI bottom ash quantitatively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the weathering of MSWI bottom ash is a complicated process, which is relevant interactively to the formation of secondary minerals and the pH neutralization.
the weathering of MSWI bottom ash is a complex process and that the weathering indices of natural rock profiles are not directly applicable to MSWI bottom ash.

the application of mineralogical weather indices to fresh/weathered MSW residues could not explain leachate pH or leaching concentration of major and trace element quantitatively, but it could be useful to identify fresh/landfilled bottom ash and to roughly estimate landfilling time.
The main takeaway from our work is that

mineralogical weather indices for natural rock are useful to describe the weathering process of fresh/landfilled bottom ash and that they could not be directly applied to leaching behaviors of component elements.
the mineralogical indices of natural rock weathering are useful to distinguish fresh and land filled MSWI bottom ash quantitatively and qualitatively.
the weathering indices for fresh and weathered MSWI bottom ashes were successfully evaluated by the weathering indices developed for natural rock.
